urgency.h: They Think You Can't Prove It. We Do This Every Week.
urgency.sub: Nobody says "we're firing you because you're 52" out loud. They say "restructuring." Proving what they actually meant is our job.

cards.t: Pretext is a pattern, not a confession
cards.p: Ten years of great reviews, then a write-up three weeks after you asked for leave. The younger replacement. The "budget cut" that only hit the one person with a disability. Juries see through it — when a lawyer lays it out.

cards.t: Retaliation makes it worse for them
cards.p: Complaining about discrimination is protected. If they cut your hours, iced you out, or fired you after you spoke up, that's a second illegal act — with its own damages.
You have a filing window with the Civil Rights Department — and every week you wait, emails get purged and witnesses move on. A preservation demand from us stops the bleeding.

results.label: Employment settlements by one partner since 2023

result_highlight: California's Fair Employment and Housing Act is one of the strongest anti-discrimination laws in the country: unlimited emotional-distress damages, punitive damages, and mandatory attorney's fees when you win. It applies to employers with as few as five employees.

value.h: What California Law Says They Owe You
value.sub: Not "maybe." These are the damages the Fair Employment and Housing Act puts on the table when an employer breaks it.

items.p: Back pay from the day it happened, plus front pay for what you'll lose while you rebuild — raises, bonuses, health coverage, and retirement included.
Being singled out, humiliated, and pushed out because of who you are does real damage. California juries award real money for it — with no cap.
When a company acts with malice — or knew what a manager was doing and let it continue — the jury can award punitive damages meant to punish.
In some cases, the court can order the job, the promotion, or the accommodation you were denied.
Under FEHA the employer pays your legal fees when you win — which is exactly why we charge you nothing unless we do.

faq.a: Race, color, national origin, ancestry, religion, age (40+), sex, gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy and related conditions, disability and medical conditions, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, and requesting or taking protected leave. Being punished for complaining about any of it is retaliation — also illegal.

faq.q: They never said anything discriminatory out loud. Can I still prove it?
faq.a: Yes. Most discrimination cases are proven by pattern: timing, comparisons to how others were treated, shifting explanations, and who replaced you. That's the work we do.

faq.q: I asked for an accommodation and things went downhill. Is that a case?
faq.a: Often, yes. California requires employers to engage in a good-faith "interactive process" and provide reasonable accommodations for disabilities, medical conditions, and pregnancy. Refusing, stalling, or punishing you for asking is actionable.
